newsitem.title: USA: Emergent sees Q2 net meeting estimates.
newsitem.headline: Emergent sees Q2 net meeting estimates.

text.p: Emergent Group Inc said Friday it expects its net income for the second quarter ended June 30 to be in the range of analysts' expectations for the period, if not higher.

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jack Sterling, in a talk with investors, said the company based its expectations on continued strong growth in loan origination volume, positive delinquency trends, the results of quarterly securitization and loan sales. He said final results are expected to be released the week of July 21.
First Call's consensus estimate of Emergent's second quarter 1997 net income per share is $0.18.

Sterling, who spoke to investors at the Wheat First Butcher Singer 1997 Nantucket Conference, said loan production for the second quarter increased 171 percent to $309 million from $114 million for the year-ago period.

He said the company sold or securitized $253.7 million of loans in the second quarter of 1997, leaving $257.1 million of loans on its balance sheet. Loans sold in the quarter were up 102 percent from the prior quarter and 171 percent from the second quarter of 1996, he said.
Delinquencies over 30 days have decreased to 6.32 percent as of June 30, from 7.24 percent of total unguaranteed serviced loans at March 31, he added.

Mortgage loan delinquencies over 30 days dropped to 6.57 percent as of June 30 from 7.19 percent at March 31, he said.. Small business delinquecies declined to 3.20 percent from 6.08 percent while those for auto loans rose to 10.82 percent from 10.11 percent, he said.
